channel.title: DevPulse · Security
channel.description: Daily security stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: ESauron detects hidden cameras through memory-generated electromagnetic signals
item.description: ESauron stimulates scene changes and detects the resulting electromagnetic patterns from camera memory activity to locate wired, wireless and offline spy cameras. The approach is a technically interesting example of sensing device behavior through side-channel emissions.

item.title: Telegram Desktop link handling enabled file theft through IPC injection
item.description: A crafted link injects commands through Telegram Desktop's local socket, then invokes an internal URI that reads and sends a file without checking authorization. The chain enabled arbitrary file theft and account takeover; version 7.2.9 fixes it.

item.title: Vulnerable Android dialers can enable one-click MMI execution
item.description: The reported flaws let an attacker trigger MMI codes through a vulnerable dialer with little or no user interaction. The issue illustrates how app permissions and dialer handling can expose sensitive phone functions.

item.title: Wiping secrets can leave extra copies in compiled code
item.description: The article shows how adding a zeroization call can result in more secret copies, including a `memset` example that the compiler optimizes away. Engineers handling secrets need to reason about generated code, not just source-level wipes.

item.title: C code can call execve without naming the function
item.description: A student describes trying to get shell execution in a grading sandbox that rejects disallowed function names, and notes that the checker parses code with Clang. The technique is relevant to engineers designing source-based restrictions around untrusted code.

item.title: Pixel 11’s missing memory tagging may block a full GrapheneOS port
item.description: GrapheneOS says the Pixel 11 series lacks the ARM hardware memory tagging support needed to complete its port, a feature the project uses to harden the OS and kernel. The case shows how device-level security features constrain hardened software.

item.title: Attackers hijacked three country domains to obtain counterfeit TLS certificates
item.description: Control of the .gh, .sl and .as domains let attackers alter DNS records, pass domain-control checks and obtain unauthorized certificates for major services. The incident highlights how weaknesses in domain administration can threaten the certificate trust chain.

item.title: OpenSSH 10.6 disables its LZ77 coder to mitigate side-channel leaks
item.description: OpenSSH 10.6 disables the LZ77 dictionary coder to mitigate side-channel leaks, adds a hybrid post-quantum signature algorithm and plans more frequent releases amid AI-assisted bug reports. Operators should note the security change and its effect on compression.

item.title: Misuse of legitimate access exposes 8.8 million Danish residents’ data
item.description: Unauthorized users misused a company’s lawful access to Denmark’s CPR system to obtain personal data on about 8.8 million people. The incident highlights the risk of abuse through authorized integrations.

item.title: OpenSSH plans more frequent releases as AI-assisted bug reports rise
item.description: OpenSSH says it is receiving many security reports found or assisted by AI, and will release more often to get fixes to users sooner. The shift highlights how AI-assisted discovery can change security triage and release cadence.

item.title: Cloudflare Containers vulnerability exposed residual disk blocks across tenants
item.description: Researchers showed that a customer could recover residual disk blocks previously used by Containers on the same host, though they could not target a particular customer or workload. The cross-tenant isolation failure is directly relevant to engineers operating multi-tenant infrastructure.

item.title: A small Linux container demonstrates namespaces, capabilities and syscall restrictions
item.description: The walkthrough builds a minimal container for untrusted code and examines namespaces, capabilities, mounts, system calls and resource limits, while warning against treating the minimal setup as production-safe. Understanding these isolation controls helps engineers reason about sandbox boundaries and what must be restricted.

item.title: Reversible ballot shuffles exposed the order of 98.9% of Georgia primary ballots
item.description: The author says a reversible scanner-record shuffle and public voting logs let them reconstruct the order of 98.9% of in-person ballots in Georgia’s May 2026 primary; some states had not applied the fix. It shows how metadata can undermine ballot anonymity.

item.title: C2PA metadata can make a photoshopped image appear to predate an event
item.description: A photoshopped image uses C2PA metadata to appear to show lottery numbers before the draw, despite its verifiable signature and timestamp. The demonstration highlights why signed provenance alone may not establish when an image was actually created.

item.title: Two SMTP parsing flaws enabled email spoofing through Apple iCloud
item.description: A case study describes two email spoofing vulnerabilities in iCloud’s SMTP infrastructure and revisits SMTP smuggling after implementations adopted fixes. It offers a concrete look at how parser behavior can undermine email identity checks.

item.title: SequenceHash and SequenceMAC prevent ambiguous multihash encodings
item.description: The open specification introduces hash constructions intended to avoid attacks on ambiguous input encodings, working with hash functions such as SHA-2, BLAKE, and RIPEMD rather than only Keccak. The approach is relevant to engineers building secure cryptographic protocols and systems.

item.title: Xray-core faces a certificate-verification bypass allegation
item.description: A reporter alleges that Xray-core concealed a certificate-verification bypass for half a year, involving its pinned-peer-certificate feature. Proxy users and maintainers should assess whether certificate checks can be bypassed in their own configurations.

item.title: Rust WebP decoder aims to improve memory safety and speed
item.description: The wpd decoder is written in Rust and claims better single-threaded performance and parallel scaling than libwebp, targeting a format implicated in a widely exploited memory-safety flaw. It is relevant to engineers balancing parser security and throughput.

item.title: Kernel security team responds to a surge in LLM-assisted bug reports
item.description: Greg Kroah-Hartman discussed how the kernel security team is handling a flood of reports after LLMs made security bugs easier to identify, with a central message of “don’t panic.” The response offers relevant context for teams managing security triage as report volume grows.

item.title: Court blocks Utah law requiring websites to identify or block VPN users
item.description: A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction against Utah’s age-verification law, which would require websites to block VPN users or identify their physical locations. The ruling highlights the technical and privacy costs of trying to identify traffic masked by VPNs.

item.title: A malicious Git post-checkout hook targets developer credentials
item.description: A project inquiry used a shared Dropbox folder containing a hidden .git directory to try to run code on the target’s laptop. Developers reviewing unfamiliar repositories should treat hooks and project files as untrusted.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers adds Web Crypto support for ML-KEM and ML-DSA
item.description: Workers adds ML-KEM-768/1024 and ML-DSA-44/65/87 APIs behind a compatibility flag, including key encapsulation, signatures, and JWK import and export. The primitives let developers test post-quantum integrations without bundling a separate implementation, though they are not a full migration path.

item.title: Debian upgrades rsync to 3.5.0 to address 33 CVEs
item.description: Debian chose a version upgrade over backporting 33 CVE fixes, citing lower risk; the update also changes handling of operator-supplied paths through untrusted symlinks. Operators should review compatibility implications before upgrading.

item.title: Unsigned login token could have enabled SQL access to 17.3 trillion Microsoft records
item.description: A missing token-signature check let the researcher claim an administrator identity and submit unauthorized SQL queries to an internal analytics service; the 17.3 trillion-row reach is described as potential impact. The case shows how a single authentication check can affect a broad data service.

item.title: Stale branch predictions enable Spectre-v2 attacks in JIT engines
item.description: Branch Target Reuse exploits stale indirect branch predictions that can survive code-cache repopulation, creating a speculative execute-after-free primitive; the researchers built two Linux kernel exploits. JIT and runtime engineers should consider how generated-code reuse interacts with CPU speculation.

item.title: Cloudflare seeks public CA status and plans to serve post-quantum certificates
item.description: Cloudflare has applied to major root programs and agreed to acquire a broadly trusted root from GlobalSign, with post-quantum certificates as a stated goal. A new large-scale certificate issuer could affect the trust infrastructure and migration paths web services depend on.

item.title: Attackers used ESXi exploits after likely entering through a SonicWall VPN
item.description: Huntress reports a December 2025 intrusion involving ESXi exploits and assesses that access likely began through a compromised SonicWall VPN; responders stopped the activity. The case underscores that virtualization isolation and basic perimeter access both matter.

item.title: AI-era vulnerability disclosures doubled from January to August 2026
item.description: Google reports monthly disclosures rising from 5,045 in January 2026 to 10,740 in August, while average monthly exploitation rose from 10.5 in 2025 to 18 in 2026. Security teams can use the trend data to reassess vulnerability triage and response capacity.

item.title: PS5 exploit chain combines a WebKit corruption bug with a kernel UAF race
item.description: The chain uses JavaScriptCore information leaks and a structured-clone mismatch to corrupt a typed array, then an aio_multi_wait use-after-free race for kernel read/write. Its firmware range and instability notes make the exploit mechanics concrete, though console security is peripheral to this digest.

item.title: A Brazilian federal system exposed records for more than 200 million people
item.description: A discovered vulnerability gave access to records containing identity documents, addresses and other personal information, including witness-protection status. The disclosure highlights the stakes of security testing in systems holding national-scale data.

item.title: Nine fake npm packages spread a Linux worm through preinstall hooks
item.description: The packages download and run a worm during installation, which installs a Tor-accessible backdoor disguised as a systemd font service. The chain highlights the risk of malicious dependencies executing on developer Linux machines.

item.title: Two OnePlus flaws let an untrusted app gain root with no special permissions
item.description: The author chained two issues to reach uid 0 with all Linux capabilities from an ordinary APK, then verified the exploit on a OnePlus 15. The write-up is a concrete example of how flaws combine to defeat a device’s app boundary.

item.title: Cloudflare tests WAFs by having LLMs mutate attack payloads
item.description: Cloudflare describes a dynamic test in which an LLM probes running applications using only selected HTTP responses, iterating on payloads without source-code or rule access. This offers a way to think about testing defenses against adaptive attackers, though the excerpt gives no results.

item.title: Cloudflare Application Profiles enforce policies from HTTP request structure
item.description: Application Profiles analyze HTTP request structure and format to identify deviations and enforce a positive security policy. The approach gives security teams another way to reduce attack surface beyond relying only on patching and attack signatures.

item.title: Cloudflare adds beta protection against post-quantum IPsec downgrade attacks
item.description: Cloudflare says it worked with the IETF on an IPsec downgrade mitigation and made it available in beta across its IPsec products. Teams migrating network protocols to post-quantum cryptography should account for downgrade risks as well as new algorithms.

item.title: ShinyHunters bypassed PeopleSoft WAF rules with a URL-encoded path
item.description: The campaign encoded one character in the PeopleSoft endpoint path, bypassing literal-path WAF rules before the application decoded and routed the request. The mismatch is a useful reminder that filtering and application routing must normalize paths consistently.

item.title: LuaRocks.org RCE was exploited, prompting a full credential reset
item.description: After finding that an RCE had been exploited, LuaRocks rebuilt its server and revoked credentials, sessions, and exposed secrets. The incident is a useful reminder of the blast radius of compromise at a software package service.

item.title: TEE rollback can make MPC signers reuse nonce shares and leak keys
item.description: A malicious host can roll back a signer’s filesystem after a pre-signature is deleted, causing nonce-share reuse and exposing a private key share. The guidance treats TEEs as defense in depth and emphasizes attestation tied to participant identities.

item.title: CI/CD attacks exploit cache poisoning, OIDC tokens, and mutable action tags
item.description: The guidance describes attacks on developer tools and build pipelines, including GitHub Actions cache poisoning, OIDC token extraction, and changing action tags to publish compromised packages. These tactics expose risks in trusted automation with elevated privileges.

item.title: A Twitch overlay chain turned chat text into code execution on a streamer’s PC
item.description: Viewer text ran as raw HTML in an OBS browser source, where an unsandboxed Chromium renderer and a V8 bug enabled native code execution. The chain illustrates how an untrusted-content feature can expose a desktop host.

item.title: Radicle protocol flaws expose traffic and let attackers impersonate peers
item.description: Radicle’s protocol lacks expected confidentiality and has broken peer authentication, allowing an on-path attacker to read traffic and impersonate an allowed node to fetch private repositories. The flaws show why peer allow-lists do not protect against compromised network paths.
